By way of this judgment, I shall decide the present suit filed by the plaintiff for recovery of Rs.
45,32,521/- along with pendente lite and future interest @ 24% per annum from the date of filing of the suit till its realization.
CASE OF THE PLAINTIFF 2.

It is the case of the plaintiff that it is a company engaged in the manufacture and supply of non-woven fabrics, bags and printed fabrics having its office at 54-A, Gupta House, Sainik Farms,
Khanpur, New Delhi-110062.
3.

It is further the case of the plaintiff that the present suit has been instituted by it through its Authorized Representative, Sh. Dheeraj Kumar and the defendant firm namely M/s Gargi Packaging, through its responsible officers/ partners (defendant nos. 2 to 5), approached the plaintiff at its New Delhi office for purchase of non-woven fabric on a wholesale basis.

It is further averred that upon the representations and assurances of the defendants, the plaintiff agreed to supply goods to the defendant firm on a credit basis through a running account maintained in the ordinary course of business.

4. The plaintiff further avers that pursuant to the oral purchase orders placed by the defendants at the plaintiff's office, non-woven fabric and allied goods worth 72,27,472/- were supplied during the financial year 2011- 2012.
It is further averred that against the said supplies, the defendants made payments aggregating to 48,18,446/-, leaving an outstanding balance of 24,09,026/- at the end of the said financial year.

5. It is further averred that during the financial year 2012- 2013, the plaintiff continued to supply goods worth 46,20,119/- to the defendants and including the outstanding balance from the previous year, the total liability of the defendants during the said period stood at 70,29,032/-.
6. According to the plaintiff, the defendants paid a sum of 40,56,887/- during the financial year 2012-2013, leaving a balance of 29,72,145/-.

It is further averred that the last payment of 2,50,000/- was made by the defendants on 26.02.2013 through Bank of Baroda, Current Account No. 1059050000070 and thereafter no further payment was made by the defendants.

7. It is further the case of the plaintiff that the defendants issued the requisite 'C-Forms' on 11.06.2013 and had been making payments earlier through cheques and bank transfers, though several cheques issued by the defendants were dishonoured on presentation.
It is further averred that despite repeated demands, the due outstanding amount remained unpaid.

It is further averred that as per the ledger maintained by the plaintiff in the ordinary course of business, a sum of 29,72,145/- remained due and payable as on 30.04.2013.
8.

The plaintiff further asserts that as per the terms and conditions mentioned in the invoices and as reiterated in the legal notices, the defendants are liable to pay interest @ 18% per annum on the Greatech Telecom Technologies Pvt Ltd vs Gargi Packaging And Ors on 30 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49937044/
2 outstanding amount.

9. It is further stated that the plaintiff also issued legal notices dated 03.06.2013 and 08.07.2013 to the defendants calling upon the defendants to clear the outstanding dues, however, despite service of the said notices, no payment was made.

10. The plaintiff further states that police complaints were lodged against the defendants, wherein defendant no.2 allegedly admitted non-payment of the outstanding amount and failure to return the goods.

It is further stated that a criminal complaint under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was also filed before the Ld. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, South District, Saket Courts, New Delhi, which is stated to be pending adjudication.

The plaintiff has further claimed interest for a period of 2 years and 11 months amounting to 15,60,376/- @ 18% per annum, thereby raising a total claim of 45,32,521/-.
12.

Accordingly, the plaintiff has prayed for a decree for recovery of 45,32,521/- along with pendente lite and future interest @ 24% per annum from the date of filing of the suit till its realization along with costs of the suit.
PROCEEDINGS BEFORE THE COURT 13.
Defendant No.3/ Mahesh Giri and Defendant No. 5/ Smt. Asha Giri were duly served.

However,
neither Defendant No.3/ Mahesh Giri and Defendant No. 5/ Smt. Asha Giri appeared before the court nor any appearance was put on their behalf.
Consequently, vide order dated 20.07.2016, the Defendant No.3/ Mahesh Giri and Defendant No. 5/ Smt. Asha Giri defendant were proceeded ex parte.

Further in view of the statement given by the plaintiff qua deletion of the Defendant No.4/Yashpal Tyagi, the said Defendant No. 4/ Yashpal Tyagi was deleted from array of the parties vide vide order dated 23.08.2017.

Accordingly fresh amended memo of parties was filed by the plaintiff reflecting M/s Gargi Packaging as Defendant No.1, Sh Hansa Giri S/o Sh Kewal Giri as Defendant No.2, Sh Mahesh Giri S/o Sh Kewal Giri as Defendant No.3 and Smt Asha Giri, W/o Hansa Giri as Defendant No.4.

CASE OF THE DEFENDANTS (WRITTEN  STATEMENT FILED ON BEHALF OF DEFENDANT  NO. 1 AND 2)
14.
The defendants no.1 and 2 filed a joint written statement contesting the suit and raised several preliminary objections.
It is their case that defendant no.1 is a proprietorship concern and defendant no.2 is the sole proprietor thereof.

It is contended that defendant nos.3 to 5 have been wrongly arrayed as parties without disclosing any legal liability and that the suit suffers from misjoinder of parties and is liable to be dismissed on this ground alone.

sentences.text: The defendants have further objected to the maintainability of the suit on the ground of limitation.

It is averred that in a complaint lodged by the plaintiff before the SHO, PS Neb Sarai, the plaintiff itself stated that the last business transaction took place between 16.04.2012 and 26.10.2012 and therefore, the present suit is barred by limitation.

16. It is further the case of the defendants that the plaintiff had earlier initiated criminal proceedings against them under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., pursuant to which the defendants joined the enquiry and furnished their statements.
According to the defendants, the enquiry officer found the complaint to be not maintainable.

It is alleged that the criminal proceedings as well as the present suit have been instituted with mala fide intent to harass and extort money, and that the plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands and has suppressed material facts.

17. The defendants further allege contradictions between the invoices referred to by the plaintiff in the police complaint and those filed along with the plaint, contending that the same demonstrates falsity in the plaintiff's case.
It is also alleged that the ledger accounts, invoices and transport receipts relied upon by the plaintiff are false, fabricated and manipulated.
18. It is specifically denied that any amount is due or payable by the defendants to the plaintiff.
On this basis, it is contended that the suit is without cause of action and liable to be rejected.

The defendants have also objected to the description of parties, stating that the plaintiff has incorrectly mentioned the name of the father of defendant no.2 namely Sh. Kewal Giri as a partner, whereas he had expired in the year 1974.
According to the defendants, this further reflects suppression of facts and misrepresentation.

19. On merits, the defendants have denied the averments made in the plaint regarding the plaintiff's business status, the authority of its alleged Authorized Representative, the existence of any credit arrangement with the Plaintiff, supply of goods by the Plaintiff to the Defendants as claimed or the maintenance of any running account of the Plaintiffs in respect of the goods supplied to the defendants.
20.
It is the specific stand of the defendants that the plaintiff had approached them for sale of raw material and that defendant nos.3 to 5 have no connection whatsoever with defendant no.1.
The defendants assert that all payments for goods supplied were duly made and that no outstanding amount remains payable.

21. The defendants have categorically denied the figures of supply, payments, outstanding balance and interest claimed by the plaintiff, asserting that the accounts maintained by the plaintiff are not fair, correct or reliable.
The alleged last payment dated 26.02.2013 and the outstanding balance of 29,72,145/- were also specifically denied.
22. The defendants have also denied liability to pay any interest or damages and have refuted the allegation that they were habitual defaulters.
It is contended that the defendants themselves have suffered harassment and mental agony on account of the criminal proceedings and the present litigation.

SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF THE DEFENDANTS 62.

Conversely, learned counsel for the defendants argued that the plaintiff has failed to prove actual delivery of goods, as the delivery receipts relied upon do not disclose the name of the driver or the person who allegedly received the goods.
It is contended that the ledger statements produced by the plaintiff are computer-generated documents and are not supported by a valid certificate under Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act.
It is further contended that PW-1 is neither the author nor the custodian of such records.
63. Learned counsel for the defendants further submitted that defendant no. 3 has no concern with the business of defendant no. 1 and therefore the suit suffers from mis- joinder of parties.
It is argued that the defendants had already made full payment to the plaintiff during the course of business and no amount remains outstanding.

Counsel for the defendant further contended that the suit is barred by limitation, asserting that the last transaction between the parties took place in the year 2012 and the suit has been filed in the year 2016.

Lastly, it is argued that the plaintiff has not approached the Court with clean hands and has relied upon manipulated ledger accounts and false notices and accordingly it is contended that the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be dismissed.

29,72,145/- by placing on record invoices, delivery receipts, statutory C-Forms acknowledging deliver of goods, ledger account statements of the defendant maintained by the plaintiff,
dishonoured cheques, police complaints and legal notices.
The C-Forms issued by the defendants constitute strong and unimpeachable evidence acknowledging the transactions and delivery of the goods.
The defendants, despite opportunity, have failed to rebut this documentary evidence or to prove the alleged payment.
Apparently, a bare plea of full payment, unsupported by any material cannot dislodge the plaintiff's case.

Consequently, the liability of the defendants to the tune of Rs.
29,72,145/- towards the plaintiff as on 31.03.2013 stands duly established.
75. Now coming to the claims of 45,32,521/- put forth by the plaintiff.

The plaintiff in the present suit, apart from the due outstanding amount of 29,72,145/- towards the sale of goods as on 31.03.2013, has also claimed pre suit interest for a period of 2 years and 11 months on the same,
amounting to 15,60,376/- @ 18% per annum, thereby raising the total claim of 45,32,521/- and is further also claiming pendente lite and future interest @ 24% per annum on the claimed from the date of filing of the suit till its realization.
76. The pre-suit interest and post suit interest as claimed by the plaintiff is a more delicate question.

The plaintiff has admittedly added in his claim a pre suit interest @ 18% per annum on the due amount of Rs29,72,145/- and is further seeking interest at @24% pendente lite and future interest per annum stating that the same is terms and condition of the invoices and as per the legal notice sent by the plaintiff to the defendants.

It is true that while such stipulations regarding interest often appear on commercial invoices, however interestingly in the invoices Ex. PW-1/7 to Ex. PW1/10 placed on record by the plaintiff there is no such stipulation regarding levying of the interest in case of any default/ delay in payment.
Evidently courts are not bound to mechanically enforce the rate of interest claimed by the plaintiff.
Section 34 of the CPC vests discretion in the Court to determine what rate is reasonable and just in the given circumstances.

sentences.text: It is also trite law that the rate and period of interest cannot be applied mechanically or at an unreasonably high rate without any rationale.
It is the duty of the court to ensure that while the claimant is fairly compensated, the award of interest does not become punitive or unduly burdensome on the defendant.

Therefore, awarded interest needs to be compensatory rather than penal and should be determined in a manner that balances both fairness and financial impact,
taking into account the economic prudence in the specific facts of each case.
78.
In the present case, as discussed earlier even in the bills Ex. PW-1/7 to Ex. PW1/10 no standard penalty clause is printed as terms of the invoices.

Further there is nothing on record to suggest that the claimed pre suit interest amount of 18% per annum or the post suit interest amount of 24% per annum is specifically negotiated or mutually agreed rate of interest between the parties.
There is no separate written agreement or correspondence indicating that the defendant consciously accepted this rate as a term of the contract.
The transaction evidently is a simple sale of goods and not a financing arrangement.

79. Furthermore, the absence of a negotiated agreement shows that the claimed pre suit interest amount of 18% per annum or the claimed post suit interest amount of 24% per annum is more in the nature of a penal stipulation rather than a genuine pre-estimate of financial loss.
Therefore, the claimed pre suit interest rate of 18% per annum or the post suit interest of 24% per annum cannot be justified as a fair measure of compensation.

Further it is evident from the discussion above that the outstanding liability of the defendants towards the sale of goods by the plaintiff is only 29,72,145/- which remained outstanding as on 31.03.2013.

Therefore, considering the nature of the transaction and the absence of a separately negotiated agreement, this Court holds that an interest rate of 6% per annum would be fair, reasonable and just as pendentelite and future interest only on outstanding liability of the defendants i.e. 29,72,145/-.
Such a rate adequately compensates the plaintiff for the delay in payment without imposing an undue or penal burden on the defendant.

80. Accordingly, the plaintiff shall also be entitled to interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the principal outstanding sum of 29,72,145/, applicable as pendente lite and future interest till realization.

I.

The plaintiff is entitled to a money decree for a sum of  Rs. 29,72,145/- (Rupees Twenty Nine Lakhs Seventy Two Thousand One Hundred and Fourty Five Only)
against the defendant.

II. The plaintiff shall further be entitled to interest at the rate of 6% per annum on the aforesaid principal amount, to be calculated as pendente lite interest and future interest until realization.
III. The plaintiff shall also be entitled to costs of the suit.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
